scenario: AITA for refusing to attend my friend's second wedding and being unsupportive overall? | Excuse me if I make any mistakes. I was the bridesmaid for the wedding between Dia and Jake. I have known both of them since I was little, in fact, I was the one who introduced them to each other. Dia was my neighbor and Jake was the son of my mother's colleague, they were like brother and sister to me and we have been close. After dating for 6 years and married for 2 years, Jake passed away suddenly from a fever last March. This year January, Dia announced that she was to be married again, and she wanted me to attend her wedding, date is not set but very likely in a couple of months. I had no idea that Dia even had another boyfriend till she announced it despite being close to her. It was barely a year after Jake's death I could not believe nor accept that she was already having her second marriage. When I tried to ask, Dia only said that she was going to move forward and leave the painful memories behind. I turned down the invitation. Dia was upset that I couldn't be supportive for her new found happiness, she said that I am important to her and she wanted me to be there for her, to show her the love and support like when she and Jake got together. I couldn't. I love Dia, and I love Jake too. It just didn't sit well with me that Dia moved on so quickly and I was angry at her and felt sorry for Jake. Jake and Dia are the only true couple in my eyes. Her friends are saying that I am being selfish making it all about myself and not for the bride, that I should be a true friend and be happy and supportive for her. AITA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to refuse attending my friend Dia's second wedding, especially since I was her bridesmaid in her first marriage to Jake. Let me start by understanding the situation better. First, I've known both Dia and Jake since I was little. In fact, I introduced them to each other. They were like brother and sister to me, and we've always been close. They dated for six years and were married for two years before Jake passed away suddenly last March from a fever. That was a really tough time for all of us. Now, this January, Dia announced that she's going to marry again and wants me to attend her wedding, even though the date isn't set yet. I didn't even know she had another boyfriend until she told me. It's barely been a year since Jake's death, and I can't believe or accept that she's already moving on to a second marriage. When I tried to ask her about it, she said she's moving forward and leaving the painful memories behind. I turned down the invitation, which made Dia upset because she felt I wasn't supportive of her new happiness. She said I'm important to her and wanted me to be there for her, showing her love and support like when she and Jake got married. I love Dia, and I also loved Jake. It just doesn't sit well with me that Dia moved on so quickly, and I feel angry at her and sorry for Jake. In my eyes, Jake and Dia are the only true couple. Her friends are saying that I'm being selfish, making it all about myself and not for the bride, and that I should be a true friend and be happy and supportive for her. So, is it right or wrong for me to refuse attending her second wedding and being unsupportive overall? I need to think about this carefully. First, I need to understand my own feelings. Why am I upset about Dia remarrying so soon after Jake's death? Is it because I feel that Jake's memory is being dishonored, or is it because I'm not ready to accept that Dia is moving on? Maybe I'm projecting my own grief onto Dia, expecting her to feel the same way I do. On the other hand, Dia is trying to move forward with her life, which is a natural part of the grieving process. Everyone grieves differently, and what's right for me might not be right for her. She might feel that remarrying is a way to find happiness again after such a tragic loss. But I'm also feeling that by refusing to attend her wedding, I'm being unsupportive. Friends are saying that I'm being selfish, and I need to consider whether that's true. Am I prioritizing my own feelings over Dia's need for support during this important time in her life? I also need to think about the impact of my decision on our friendship. If I refuse to attend her wedding, will that cause a rift between us? Or can we still maintain our friendship despite this disagreement? Moreover, I need to consider what it means to be a supportive friend. Does being supportive mean attending her wedding and showing happiness for her, even if I don't feel it? Or does it mean respecting her decision and giving her the space she needs, even if that means not attending? I also wonder if there's a middle ground. Maybe I can attend the wedding but in a way that honors both Dia and Jake. For example, I could wear something that reminds me of Jake or find a way to acknowledge his memory during the ceremony. Another thing to consider is communication. Have I talked to Dia about why I'm feeling this way? Maybe if I express my feelings openly, we can find a way to understand each other better. It's possible that Dia doesn't realize how much her decision is affecting me, and a honest conversation could help bridge the gap. I also need to reflect on whether my feelings are healthy or if I'm holding onto grief in a way that's preventing me from supporting Dia. It's important to process my own emotions so that I can be there for my friend without letting my grief control my actions. In the end, I need to decide what's best for both me and Dia. Am I willing to compromise and attend her wedding to support her, even if it's difficult for me? Or is it more important for me to honor my own feelings and boundaries, even if that means not attending? This is a tough situation, and I need to weigh the pros and cons carefully. It's important to respect both my feelings and Dia's needs, and find a balance that allows our friendship to thrive despite this disagreement.
